claim_under_test: Things can be folded and reduced LOSSLESSLY, not merely collapsed visually.
subject: fold() / dissolve() in foundry/room/space-core.js

method.fixture: S.seedFurnisher() — the module's own seed, not a hand-built model
method.compared: the sorted set of every node id, and every node's parent, before vs after
method.not_compared: x/y/w/h geometry, port arrays, operator payloads (see limitation below)

verdict.basis: The id set and the parent of every node are identical before fold and after dissolve. Nothing is copied: fold() re-parents existing nodes (space-core.js:172) and dissolve() re-parents them back and removes only its own cassette (space-core.js:179-180). There is no shadow model to drift from, which is exactly what ROOM release v0.4 law 3 asserts.
verdict.law_confirmed: FOLD MUTATES STRUCTURE, NOT A SHADOW MODEL — foundry/room/release.json v0.4

limitations: Geometry (x/y/w/h) is computed fresh by fold() from the children's bounds; a fold/dissolve round-trip is NOT expected to restore original coordinates, and this test does not claim it does.
Ports are recomputed by boundaryPorts(); equality after round-trip is not asserted here.
Only the seed model (7 nodes) was exercised. A larger or cyclic model is untested.
This proves the STRUCTURE round-trips. It does not prove the six faces are sufficient to generate a surface, which is a separate and unproven claim.
next: If the fold is to be the reduction primitive for the whole field, the same test must be run over a subtree of the LIVE manifest, not just the seed.
